title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It is often used to make data easy to explore and visualize.

title: Orthogonality in PCA
text: In PCA, the principal components are orthogonal to each other. This means that the dot product of any two different principal components is zero.

title: Orthogonality of PC1 and PC2
text: If PC1 and PC2 are orthogonal, what is the dot product of PC1 and PC2?

title: Variance in PCA
text: Each principal component in PCA captures the maximum possible variance in the data, given the constraint that it is orthogonal to the preceding components.

title: Variance of PC1 and PC2
text: Which principal component captures more variance, PC1 or PC2?
